proposer.mechanism: Replace AFG's hard 10s window + single threshold + immediate _position_flat=True reset on skip with: (1) an EMA-decayed signed aggressor flow (half-life ~5s) so the signal degrades smoothly rather than flickering at the window edge; (2) a two-tier gate — skip only when |ema_flow| exceeds threshold AND directional persistence (fraction of last K=5 trades on the adverse side) >= 0.6; (3) replace the post-skip anti-cascade reset with a short cool-down: after a skip, the next 2.0 seconds of incoming orders are submitted unconditionally, after which gating resumes. Skip only opens; reduce-only always submits.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: AFG leaves two distinct sources of edge on the table: (a) the hard time-window creates a step function — a trade at t=10.001s contributes 0 but at t=9.999s contributes full size, generating regime-switch noise; (b) the immediate _position_flat reset means after every skip the very next signal fires unconditionally, throwing away half the gate's information. EMA-decay smooths (a); cool-down (vs full reset) preserves more gate decisions, capturing more of the adverse-selection edge per oracle signal. Persistence-AND removes single-print noise that hard threshold fires on (a single 3-contract print at threshold=2 currently triggers a skip even if the prior 9s of flow was perfectly balanced).
proposer.why_survives_costs: Cost model is zero commission, zero slippage in this backtest (verified from results/backtest-results.json: mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0 on both base AFG and simple). Edge therefore comes entirely from realized_pnl differential. Base AFG already shows +54.2% vs simple (and +704.8% in the cached results) at ~21.6% skip rate, with broad-based date coverage (10/12 dates beat). The proposed refinements raise gate precision (fewer false skips on transient noise) and increase gate recall (cool-down vs reset captures ~2x more gate evaluations). Even a 5-10% improvement in skip precision compounds across ~100k trades.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) — preserves the signed-aggressor-flow primitive while refining the gating logic on three independent axes.
proposer.alternatives_considered: Considered: (a) imbalance-of-imbalance — second derivative of aggressor flow — rejected: noisier, no clear hypothesis for futures microstructure. (b) Quote-mid divergence — already addressed by microprice/ob-imbalance gates listed as prior work. (c) Trade-count rather than volume-weighted flow — base AFG NOTES explicitly considered and dismissed this as less informative. (d) Longer 30s window matching oracle horizon — rejected: prior runs note 60s windows pick up stale signal; we keep the short-term emphasis but smooth via EMA. (e) Asymmetric thresholds (BUY vs SELL) — rejected: oracle is symmetric (sigma=6.0 with seed=42) and no prior evidence of directional asymmetry on MESM6.

objections.text: The combined 'magnitude AND persistence>=0.6 of K=5 trades' gate is strictly stricter than base AFG's single magnitude check. Base AFG already operates at ~21.6% skip rate. Adding an AND condition mechanically reduces skip rate, which means fewer adverse-selection moments are filtered — reducing the very edge the gate captures. The proposer asserts '5-10% improvement in skip precision compounds' but does not quantify the recall loss, and the two effects can easily cancel or net negative.

The 2.0s cool-down has no empirical justification — it is chosen by intuition. With oracle signal cadence of 1.0s, a 2.0s cool-down lets ~1-2 signals pass unconditionally per skip, which is functionally near-identical to AFG's existing 'single free pass via _position_flat=True'. The claimed '~2x more gate evaluations' is overstated; the actual delta is approximately 0-1 additional gated signal per skip burst, which will not materially change behavior.

Unconsidered superior alternative: flow ACCELERATION / burst-detection. Base AFG measures the steady-state level of signed aggressor flow; the proposal smooths that with EMA. But the strongest microstructure predictor of adverse selection in a 30s-horizon oracle is a regime-CHANGE — i.e., when the recent 2-3s of trade flow is sharply more one-sided than the prior 7-8s. A ratio-based burst detector (e.g., skip when |signed_flow_recent_3s| / max(|signed_flow_full_10s|, eps) > burst_ratio AND directions agree) captures this. The proposer dismissed second-derivative variants as 'noisier' without empirical grounding and did not consider ratio-based burst forms that are inherently robust to scale. This is plausibly a larger source of edge than EMA-smoothing the existing level signal.

EMA half-life=5s vs hard 10s window: the theoretical 'edge-flicker' argument is real but unquantified. The base AFG passes strongly with the hard window, suggesting edge-flicker is empirically small. The smoothing change has weak motivation absent direct evidence.

K=5-trade persistence floor implicitly disables the gate in thin trading periods (fewer than 5 trades in the EMA window). The proposal does not specify behavior in that regime — silent fallback to unconditional submit, or hard-fail-closed? This needs to be pinned down to be falsifiable.

suggested_alternatives: Replace level-based gate with a flow ACCELERATION/burst gate: skip when recent_3s signed flow / window_10s signed flow ratio > 2.0 and signs agree (adverse direction) — captures regime change rather than steady-state imbalance, which is empirically the dominant short-horizon adverse-selection driver.

Volume-conditional adaptive threshold: scale flow_threshold by recent total (unsigned) trade volume — fixed 2-contract threshold treats a quiet 5-contract window the same as a busy 50-contract window, which is unprincipled.
criticizer.reasoning: Three of the proposal's mechanisms (EMA smoothing, persistence AND-gate, cool-down) are either marginal vs base AFG behavior or strictly stricter, with the net direction of edge change being ambiguous. A clearly superior unconsidered direction — flow acceleration / burst detection — captures regime change, which is the stronger short-horizon predictor for a 30s-horizon oracle.

proposer.mechanism: Flow-Burst Gate: maintain two rolling sums of signed aggressor flow over short (3s) and long (10s) trailing windows. Skip an open order when ALL of the following hold: (1) the short-window signed flow is adverse to the order direction (BUY order: short_flow < 0; SELL order: short_flow > 0); (2) |short_flow| >= min_burst_flow (default 2.0 contracts) — filters tiny-print noise in thin periods; (3) the burst ratio |short_flow| / max(|long_flow| - |short_flow|, eps) >= burst_ratio (default 1.5) — requires the recent 3s of adverse flow to be at least 1.5x the rate-equivalent flow of the preceding 7s, i.e., a genuine acceleration. Closing/reduce-only orders always submit. After any skip, set _position_flat=True so the next open is unconditional (anti-cascade, identical to base AFG semantics). Subscribe to trade ticks, prune by ts_event, use only data with ts_event<=order.ts_init.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG captures STATE of flow (is the 10s window currently sell-heavy?). The new algo captures CHANGE in flow (has the last 3s suddenly become sell-heavy relative to the prior 7s?). The 30s-horizon oracle signal is most likely to be wrong-priced at moments when the microstructure regime is shifting — a new aggressor wave just started — rather than during steady persistent imbalance, which typically has already been priced in by the time the oracle fires. By gating on the SECOND derivative (rate of change of signed volume), the algo skips precisely the entries that face fresh, unanticipated adverse selection.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission and zero slippage cost model (verified from results/backtest-results.json for both base AFG and simple). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG (level-based) already shows +54.2% (or +704.8% in cached results) realized_pnl vs simple — strongly positive. A ratio-based burst gate captures a sharper, more informative signal. Because the burst gate requires BOTH magnitude AND acceleration, it is naturally more selective than base AFG: lower expected skip rate (~10-15% vs AFG's 21.6%), but with higher per-skip precision (catching the actual adverse-selection moments rather than steady-state imbalance that often resolves favorably within the oracle's 30s horizon). Even if the new skip set is roughly half the size of AFG's, but with 2x the per-skip avoided loss, net P&L improves.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) — preserves the signed-aggressor-flow primitive and reduce-only/anti-cascade semantics. Replaces base AFG's level-based threshold with a ratio-based acceleration test. Adds short/long window decomposition.
proposer.alternatives_considered: Considered round 1 criticisms: (i) the simple EMA-smoothed level gate I proposed in round 1 — abandoned: criticizer correctly observed it is strictly stricter than base AFG with ambiguous net direction. (ii) Pure volume-conditional adaptive threshold (no burst component) — partially absorbed: the new min_burst_flow=2.0 floor plays the same role of suppressing thin-market noise; but a pure adaptive threshold without acceleration still measures level, not change. (iii) Higher-order acceleration (third derivative / jerk) — rejected: theoretically more sensitive but at 1-3s timescales the trade-print discretization makes higher derivatives dominated by quantization noise. (iv) Asymmetric short/long windows (e.g., 2s/15s) — defaulted to 3s/10s which matches the timescale where futures-market regime shifts are empirically observable while still allowing several trades per window.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 objections addressed: (A) MAJOR 'stricter-than-AFG gate' — pivoted to ratio/acceleration gate which is qualitatively different from base AFG (measures change, not level), not just an additional AND condition on the same measurement. (B) MAJOR 'cool-down has no empirical basis' — dropped cool-down; reverted to base AFG's _position_flat=True anti-cascade reset (proven by base AFG to be sufficient). (C) MAJOR 'flow acceleration is the superior unconsidered alternative' — adopted directly as the core mechanism. (D) MINOR 'EMA half-life unmotivated' — dropped EMA; use simple rolling sums over two clean windows. (E) MINOR 'persistence-floor thin-market behavior unspecified' — replaced with explicit min_burst_flow=2.0 floor: when |short_flow| < 2.0, do NOT skip (gate disabled in thin periods, gracefully degrading to unconditional submit).

objections.text: Formula bug in the burst-ratio denominator. The proposer states 'max(|long_flow| - |short_flow|, eps)' for the older-interval normalizer. This is NOT the older 7s interval's flow magnitude. The correct expression is max(|long_flow - short_flow|, eps): subtract the signed sums first, THEN take absolute value. With the stated (incorrect) formula, when short_flow and (long_flow - short_flow) have opposite signs, e.g., long=+1 short=+3 implies older=-2 with |older|=2, but |long|-|short|=|1|-|3|=-2 then max(-2,eps)=eps, yielding a near-infinite ratio. This causes the gate to fire spuriously during legitimate reversals. As stated, the algorithm will not behave like the described 'acceleration' gate — must use signed subtraction inside the abs.

Empirical risk: base AFG's strong PASS (+54.2%, broad-based 10/12 dates beat) implies steady-state imbalance is already a strong predictor for the configured 30s-horizon oracle. The hypothesis that 'regime change' on a 3s timescale adds material edge OVER the existing 10s level signal is plausible but untested. A pure acceleration gate may end up with a smaller, noisier skip set capturing roughly the same opportunities as base AFG (since regime changes typically produce both elevated short-window flow AND elevated long-window flow — overlap with AFG's existing skip set may be high). The proposal does not pre-commit a falsifiable test of separation.

3s short window may have high variance at MES futures cadence (~1-10 trades/sec). The ratio test could chatter at the burst_ratio=1.5 boundary even with min_burst_flow=2.0 floor. A 5s/15s split would have lower variance with the same conceptual structure. Acceptable parameter risk for a first attempt, not blocking.

suggested_alternatives: Fix the formula to max(|long_flow - short_flow|, eps) — i.e., subtract signed sums then take absolute value. This is a direct fix to the BLOCKING objection.
criticizer.reasoning: The mechanism is qualitatively distinct from base AFG and addresses round 1's superior-alternative objection. However the stated burst-ratio formula has a sign-handling bug that would cause the implementation to misbehave during legitimate reversal periods (spurious near-infinite ratios). Fix the formula and the hypothesis is ready to test.

proposer.mechanism: Flow-Burst Gate (corrected): maintain two rolling sums of signed aggressor flow over short (3s) and long (10s) trailing windows derived from a SINGLE deque of (ts_event_ns, signed_volume) tuples — short_flow is the sum over entries within 3s of order.ts_init; long_flow is the sum over entries within 10s. Skip an open order when ALL of: (1) short_flow is adverse to order direction (BUY: short_flow < 0; SELL: short_flow > 0); (2) |short_flow| >= min_burst_flow (default 2.0 contracts); (3) burst ratio |short_flow| / max(|long_flow - short_flow|, eps) >= burst_ratio (default 1.5). The denominator uses signed subtraction first: long_flow - short_flow correctly extracts the OLDER 7s interval's signed flow, then take absolute value. eps=1e-6. Closing/reduce-only orders always submit. After any skip, set _position_flat=True so next open is unconditional. Subscribe to trade ticks; ts_event<=order.ts_init at decision time.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Same as round 2: base AFG measures STATE of flow over a single 10s window; this algo decomposes that window into a recent 3s (the 'burst') and an older 7s (the 'baseline'), and skips only when the recent interval is BOTH adverse-directional AND meaningfully accelerated relative to the older interval. This captures regime-change moments rather than steady-state imbalance. The 30s-horizon oracle is hypothesized to be most often mispriced precisely at such moments — when a new wave of one-sided aggression has just started and has not yet been reflected in the oracle's signal — while steady-state imbalance is more often already priced in.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission, zero slippage cost model (verified). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. The gate is intentionally more selective than base AFG (lower expected skip rate, ~10-15% vs AFG's 21.6%) but higher per-skip precision. Falsifiable prediction: if the burst gate captures genuinely incremental edge beyond base AFG, realized_pnl on the train window will exceed base AFG's $1255.5 by at least 5% (the gate's PASS margin). If the new gate captures only an overlapping subset of base AFG's skip set (no new edge), realized_pnl will be flat or worse than base AFG and the hypothesis is falsified.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) — replaces level-based threshold with ratio-based acceleration test; preserves signed-flow primitive, reduce-only/anti-cascade semantics, trade-tick subscription pattern, and look-ahead-free deque pruning by ts_event.
proposer.alternatives_considered: Same set as round 2 plus: (v) hybrid gate (AFG-style level AND burst) — rejected because it just stacks restrictions and reduces recall without principled motivation; the goal here is to isolate the acceleration hypothesis cleanly. (vi) 5s/15s windows (criticizer suggestion) — acknowledged as plausible lower-variance choice; default 3s/10s chosen because it matches base AFG's 10s long-window for direct comparability with the base, and 3s is short enough to capture genuine regime onset. If the algorithm passes, future runs can sweep window sizes; if it fails, window choice is a secondary suspect.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 2 objections addressed: (A) BLOCKING formula bug — fixed: denominator is now max(|long_flow - short_flow|, eps) with signed subtraction inside the absolute value. The implementation will compute (long_flow - short_flow) as a single signed scalar, then abs(). (B) MAJOR empirical risk — addressed with a pre-committed falsifiable prediction: realized_pnl > base AFG by >=5% on train window if hypothesis holds; flat/worse if falsified. The risk is inherent to any first-attempt mechanism and cannot be eliminated without execution. (C) MINOR 3s window variance — acknowledged; defaulted to 3s/10s for comparability with base AFG. If this algo passes, future runs can sweep 5s/15s. If it fails, window choice is a secondary debug target.

objections.text: 3s short window variance remains a parameter-tuning risk; acknowledged by proposer as a secondary debug target if the algo fails. Acceptable.

Overlap-vs-separation between burst-skip set and base-AFG-skip set is empirically unknown until tested. The falsifiable prediction (>=5% realized_pnl improvement vs base AFG) is a clean test. Acceptable as inherent first-attempt risk.

criticizer.reasoning: Mechanism is logically coherent with the corrected formula, qualitatively distinct from base AFG (acceleration vs level), addresses round 1's superior-alternative objection and round 2's BLOCKING formula bug, and commits to a falsifiable >=5% realized_pnl improvement prediction. No remaining BLOCKING or MAJOR objections; no clearly superior untried alternative within the flow-based gating primitive family.
